title: [review] project-LICHEN-worker6-ygp9: from_bytes_for panics on complete ACK (index out-of-bounds)
description:
In `Ack::from_bytes_for`, after checking `data.len() < 2`, the code unconditionally accesses `data[2]` at `fragment.rs:265` without checking the `complete` flag. A valid 2-byte complete ACK (e.g. `[0x78, 0xc0]` from the `literal_ack_and_controls` test) would cause a panic.

Similarly, the `complete` field written by `write_to` uses bit 6 (0x40) — `(window << 7) | 0x40` — but `from_bytes_for` parses C-bit from bit 0 (`data[1] & 0x01`), so a round-trip is impossible. The parse and encode paths disagree on the bit position.

Also: `rule_id` (line 262) and `complete` (line 264) are bound but never used — `data[0]` is reused directly on line 291 instead of `rule_id`.

Pre-existing in the parent commit but not fixed here.
